finding.title: Correct streak_event_log.dart's doc comment — the real unique index is (profileId, dayUtc, eventType), not eventTimestamp
finding.rule: Evans (ubiquitous language consistency) / AG-8-adjacent (docs must match reality)

evidence.quote:
/// The single mutation method is [append]. Idempotency is enforced by
/// the UNIQUE `(profileId, eventTimestamp, eventType)` index on

finding.why: The actual Drift table declares the UNIQUE composite as (profileId, dayUtc, eventType) — eventTimestamp is not part of it, and the table's own doc comment says so explicitly ('two devices writing the same logical day-event collapse to one row'). streak_event_log.dart's code is actually correct (it computes dayUtc from eventTimestamp before inserting), but its doc comment describes a different, wrong key. This class is the write path used by core/sync/merge/streak_event_merger.dart for cross-device streak-event merge — a maintainer who trusts this comment and 'optimizes' the dedup logic around eventTimestamp instead of dayUtc would break cross-device dedup and silently duplicate streak_events rows on sync, corrupting streak counts.
finding.recommendation: Fix the doc comment to say (profileId, dayUtc, eventType), matching core/database/tables/streak_events.dart.
acceptance_criteria: streak_event_log.dart's doc comment states the same 3 columns as the @TableIndex on StreakEvents.

finding.title: Add an accessibility label to RewardConfigHeader's icon-only back button
finding.why: The back-navigation IconButton has no `tooltip` and the Icon has no semanticLabel, so a screen-reader user (TalkBack/VoiceOver) reaches this control with no announced purpose — unlike the adjacent PopupMenuButton, which gets a Flutter-provided default tooltip. This is a real, checkable AX-3 gap on a primary navigation control in a screen a parent (potentially using assistive tech) uses to configure rewards.
finding.recommendation: Add tooltip: AppLocalizations.of(context)!.<backButtonLabel> (or reuse MaterialLocalizations back-button semantics) to the IconButton.
acceptance_criteria: A widget test finds a Semantics node with a non-empty label for the back button via find.bySemanticsLabel or tester.getSemantics.

finding.title: Delete or rewire AchievementUnlockCelebration — its only trigger has been dead code since DEC-32
finding.rule: TQ-8 (regression suite must pin reachable behavior) / Fowler speculative generality
finding.why: DEC-32 replaced the auto-unlock ladder with the spend economy: evaluateUnlocksForTrack/evaluateUnlocksForGlobal are permanent no-ops, and completion_repository_impl.dart's markComplete unconditionally sets newMilestoneUnlocks to an empty list (bulkMarkComplete never produces one at all). text_display_screen.dart:704 is the ONLY caller of showForUnlockedMilestones and its `newUnlocks.isNotEmpty` guard can never be true, so the confetti/party dialog can never render for a real user. achievement_unlock_celebration_test.dart nonetheless spends ~400 of its 575 lines (title, emoji, name interpolation, auto-close timer, in-flight double-tap guard, multi-unlock ordering, RTL) driving that dialog by constructing fake RewardUnlockRecord values directly — coverage that is 100% green and gives false confidence that milestone celebrations work, whether or not product still wants this UX.
finding.recommendation: Confirm product intent: either wire a real trigger (e.g. fire when achievementsOverviewProvider flips a row from locked to unlocked) and replace the harness-only tests with one that drives the real markComplete/achievementsOverviewProvider path, or delete AchievementUnlockCelebration, its call site, and this test file, and record the removal per AG-8.
acceptance_criteria: Either an integration-level test exists that reaches showForUnlockedMilestones through the real markComplete → MarkCompletionResult.newMilestoneUnlocks path and observes a non-empty list, or `grep -rn showForUnlockedMilestones lib/` returns no hits after removal.
docs/coding-standards.md or docs/product-rules.md reflects whichever outcome is chosen (AG-8).

finding.title: Stop testing RewardSaveNoTrack/RewardSaveDuplicateThreshold — both sealed variants are unreachable post-DEC-32/GA-3
finding.rule: TQ-8 (tests must exercise the branch they claim) / Fowler speculative generality

evidence.quote:
// Manually inject a track into the state so setGlobalReward respects
      // the parameter. We can do this by mutating state via the notifier's
test('returns empty list when per-track mode but no track selected', () async {

finding.why: reward_config_controller.dart's bootstrap() hardcodes `tracks: const []` (comment: 'the form is always global and no track list is loaded'), so RewardForm.usesGlobalLadder is always true and the per-track/no-track-selected code in saveReward() is unreachable; separately, GA-3 removed the duplicate-threshold rejection entirely ('the old RewardSaveDuplicateThreshold result is no longer returned'). Despite that, 3 tests in reward_config_controller_test.dart claim to cover 'allows non-global when tracks is non-empty', 'per-track mode but no track selected', and 'RewardSaveNoTrack' but either exercise the identical tracks-empty branch under a different name or never call saveReward() at all (they assert on a hand-built RewardForm instead); a 4th test in reward_configuration_screen_l1_test.dart renders UI for a RewardSaveDuplicateThreshold result the real controller can never produce. A future revert or refactor that mangles these dead branches would ship with zero real regression coverage despite the suite appearing to test exactly that.
finding.recommendation: Remove the dead tracks/selectedTrackId/RewardSaveNoTrack/RewardSaveDuplicateThreshold machinery (and the screen's switch arm for it) now that DEC-32/GA-3 are final, deleting these 4 tests with it; or if per-track rewards are coming back, rewrite the tests to actually seed RewardForm.tracks through a real bootstrap path.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn "RewardSaveNoTrack\|RewardSaveDuplicateThreshold" lib/` returns no hits after cleanup, or a new test drives RewardForm.tracks non-empty via the real controller and asserts the branch.
No test in reward_config_controller_test.dart asserts on a hand-constructed RewardForm as a substitute for calling the notifier method the test's group() claims to cover.

finding.title: Close every in-memory Drift UserDatabase created by gamification test factories
finding.rule: TQ-6 hermetic tests / drift_memory.dart's own documented contract
finding.why: test/helpers/drift_memory.dart documents: 'Callers MUST await db.close() in tearDown to free the native resources.' These 7 factory call sites (used by ~1041+709+9+3 individual test invocations respectively) never do, so every test run leaves a live FFI-backed sqlite3 in-memory connection open until the file's isolate exits. 6 other files in this same batch (child_redemption_balance_reactive_test.dart, child_redemption_rewards_staleness_test.dart, pending_redemptions_reactive_test.dart, parent_pending_redemptions_screen_l1_test.dart, r_ga2_...test.dart, and 7 of 9 sites in child_redemption_screen_l1_test.dart) follow the contract correctly, proving it's practical here and making the gap inconsistent rather than structural.
finding.recommendation: Route each factory through addTearDown(db.close) (or the setUp/tearDown pattern parent_pending_redemptions_screen_l1_test.dart already uses correctly) so every inMemoryDb()/createTestUserDatabase() call in this feature is closed.
acceptance_criteria: grep-based Rule-0 checker: every `inMemoryDb()`/`createTestUserDatabase()` call site under test/ has a matching close() reachable from the same scope.
The 7 cited call sites each gain an addTearDown(..., .close) or equivalent.
